item.title: The Last of Us game director Bruce Straley has apologized to the God of War Laufey team after his comments about modern AAA games brought "uninvited and unnecessary negative attention."
item.description:
The Last of Us game director Bruce Straley has apologized to the God of War Laufey team after his comments about modern AAA games brought "uninvited and unnecessary negative attention."
The comments in question surfaced as part of a recently published piece by Edge magazine and saw the former Naughty Dog developer tackling the state of AAA gaming and game development. Straley initially said with a laugh that he thinks "the verbs and experiences we're delivering in the triple-A space are… I wanna say boring," before bringing God of War Laufey into the equation.
"God of War Laufey, I look at that game, and every pixel is mindblowing," he said to Edge. "The amount of work and skill that's gone into every single frame… I've made those kinds of games, and I'm still blown away. But when I actually look at what you're doing in the game? I'm not excited. And that's nothing against the God of War team. Just, across the board in triple-A, it feels like there’s no opportunity to inject fresh, innovative ideas."
The Last of Us has certainly had its influence on the state of big-budget games, so it was no surprise to see social media light up with reactions to Straley's thoughts. The former Naughty Dog lead then followed up the commotion with a thread of posts on X/Twitter, taking the opportunity to elaborate on his perspective on where the industry is at and where it's heading.
"I want to apologize to the Laufey team for dragging you all into this uninvited and unnecessary negative attention," he said. "I was trying to illustrate an industry concern and my mistake of naming your game is being used out of context and for clickbait. You don’t need this. I’m sorry.
"A journo asked me about the state of our industry. I mentioned a few concerns. One being the lack of innovation & risks taken in the AAA space. Though this isn’t the team’s fault! My fear is that our player base is getting tired of playing the same verbs for the last 20 years.
I want to apologize to the Laufey team for dragging you all into this uninvited & unnecessary negative attention. I was trying to illustrate an industry concern & my mistake of naming your game is being used out of context & for clickbait. You don’t need this. I’m sorry. 🧵 pic.twitter.com/Ri2KgfJ4yY
"My hypothesis: Our medium is unique because players are DOING a thing. There’s a different physiological response than viewers who just WATCH a movie. This requires us creators to continue to push and create new experiences, or we run the risk of diminishing players’ dopamine."
Straley then pointed to Half-Life 2, Gears of War, BioShock, Uncharted 2, and The Last of Us as a string of games that helped "set the 'modern AAA' mold," saying that each title felt like it wanted to bring new experiences to the space. He then clarified that this part of the conversation "is only one side of my concerns."
"Unfortunately the platforms that need to bring stability have eroded the ability to innovate," he continued. "The quest for [games as a service] and wanting to recreate the next Overwatch, Fortnite, Roblox, etc. is not a viable strategy and frankly shows these 'industry leaders' don't know their own brand.
"Hot take: There's a lack of good leadership, clear direction, and conviction from the people at the top, in charge of the money. (Money = stability) I believe if they understand their brand, they could have honest, inspiring conversations with creators to steer our medium to innovate."
Straley left The Last of Us studio after 18 years in September 2017. He went on to help start new game studio Wildflower Interactive in 2022 and is currently working on a new game called Coven of the Chicken Foot.
"ANYWAY… blah blah blah. I have thoughts about what's wrong and the possible serious harm done to our industry and how we might be able to fix it. But in trying to have a thoughtful conversation I stuck my foot in my mouth and mentioned Laufey, and that was my mistake. FIN (for now)."
God of War Laufey was announced as the next chapter in Santa Monica Studio's mythology-hopping action-game saga during a PlayStation State of Play presentation in June of this year. Although it's set to offer a different perspective on the universe with a story told through the eyes of Deborah Ann Woll's all-powerful Faye, it's already faced its fair share of pushback online. While some have expressed concern about playing any character other than Kratos, the studio has promised time and time again that the Ghost of Sparta will return.
God of War Laufey director Ariel Lawrence has asked skeptical fans to give Faye's story a chance ahead of its February 16, 2027 launch. While we wait to see more about how it connects to Santa Monica's gaming universe, you can read why one IGN writer felt that what we've seen so far looks too similar to Kratos' Norse saga.
Michael Cripe is a freelance writer with IGN. He's best known for his work at sites like The Pitch, The Escapist, and OnlySP. Be sure to give him a follow on Bluesky (@mikecripe.bsky.social) and Twitter (@MikeCripe).

item.title: Insomniac Games has stepped in to confirm Marvel's Wolverine contains no generative AI after a few bizarre in-game signs raised eyebrows on social media.
item.description:
Insomniac Games has stepped in to confirm Marvel's Wolverine contains no generative AI after a few bizarre in-game signs raised eyebrows on social media.
The hubbub surrounding the new PlayStation 5 exclusive's latest controversial moment kicked off when TikToker SmoothMango shared a video of their findings online (via Kotaku). Their minute-long clip focused on not one but two different bathroom signs that featured melted-together figures that look not unlike the kind of AI-generated assets audiences have attempted to train themselves to watch for.
"Folks, that looks AI-generated," SmoothMango said. "I am trying to think of a way to describe this that is not AI generation because there's no way it's a bathroom for mutants. That looks supremely suss."
At least as it's presented here, the bathroom signs certainly seem odd. With fear surrounding AI at an all-time high, fans latched onto the clip, concerned that Insomniac had used the controversial technology to help build Marvel's Wolverine.
The glitchy bathroom signs then, of course, found their way over to X/Twitter, where user Rock Solid shared images from the video. Fans again swarmed out of fear, but Insomniac has since said its Wolverine game doesn't feature a drop of genAI.
The developer's director of community and marketing, James Stevenson, replied to the X post in question to clear the air. He said "a UV map bug" is behind the strange bathroom signs, promising that Insomniac is currently working on a fix that should address any similar instances of glitchy visuals. For those who still had question marks above their heads, Stevenson was more direct: "There are no AI-generated assets in Marvel's Wolverine."
No. This is a UV map bug and we have a fix coming. There are no AI generated assets in Marvel’s Wolverine.
When Insomniac will deploy the fix remains unclear, but those worried the bathroom image may be a sign the developer used genAI for its new PS5 game can at least rest easy. It's the conclusion to yet another speed bump for the Wolverine game just days following its September 15 launch.
The first and, perhaps, most visible controversy arrived in the form of Logan's Scent Trails, which fans online had not-so-lovingly dubbed "fart gas." Thankfully, a small fix for that arrived just yesterday, with Insomniac promising to investigate a toggle option for the tracking feature as post-launch work continues. While one issue is stamped out, others are still finding reasons to be upset with the game's linear story.
Despite the backlash online, Marvel's Wolverine showed up with a seemingly strong start in terms of sales. IGN gave Insomniac's latest a 6/10 review, saying that its "slick and satisfying combat wears thin well before its conclusion, so much so that even its strong character work can't quite save it from being anything more than okay."
Michael Cripe is a freelance writer with IGN. He's best known for his work at sites like The Pitch, The Escapist, and OnlySP. Be sure to give him a follow on Bluesky (@mikecripe.bsky.social) and Twitter (@MikeCripe).

item.title: The Batman Part 2 director Matt Reeves has done his part to celebrate Batman Day by sharing a new image from the movie.
item.description:
The Batman Part 2 director Matt Reeves has done his part to celebrate Batman Day by sharing a new image from the movie.
Another September means another Batman Day, and while we're still years away from seeing Robert Pattinson reprise his role as the Caped Crusader, that isn't stopping DC Studios from celebrating. Reeves did his part to get in on the festivities by ending another months-long social media hiatus with an ominous picture from the set of The Batman Part 2 in London.
If you've seen 2022's The Batman, you'll be happy to know even this early image from the movie teases a film that will feel right at home in the saga. What we see here appears to be the back of Pattinson's Bruce Wayne as he looks ahead into what seems to be a forest-y area. We can only really see his silhouette, but it's at least yet another confirmation that The Batman Part 2 will take place in and around the snow.
"Happy Batman Day to everyone from London!" Reeves said in his post.
Is there much we can confidently say this image reveals about the plot of Reeves' new movie? Well, no, but fans are still using the holiday as an opportunity to comb through every pixel of The Batman Part 2 image in hopes of deciphering any details about its plot and characters.
One rumored villain that has stuck in the years it's taken to get The Batman sequel into theaters revolves around Gotham's secret collection of evil elites, The Court of Owls. Recently leaked set photos only stoked those flames, with fans saying that, even if there aren't any owls to be found in the new set image, they're still looking for them.
Another theory circling the new Batman image has fans arguing about the area the Dark Knight is surrounded by. Some think trees, others see smoke, and some see cars. Popular The Batman Part 2 fan account @TheBatmanSagaNW believes the setting we see here is a junkyard filled with piled-up vehicles. If that's true, it could potentially be linked to another previous rumor regarding a junkyard that will show up in the movie. IGN tweaked the image's brightness and was able to make out a location that does resemble what we'd imagine a snowy Gotham junkyard to look like.
Oh my god this shot confirms that the Junkyard set is real!!! 🦇 https://t.co/suTSmR4uve pic.twitter.com/R9Qxj3iT1L
ITS THE JUNKYARDHES IN THE JUNKYARD https://t.co/b5OdEGj7OM
It's hard to make too much out right now, and with nearly a year and a half to go before the film's release and no sign of any trailers, it will likely be a while before we learn how Reeves' set image fits into place. Following some delays, The Batman Part 2 is currently scheduled to swoop into theaters February 18, 2028.
While we wait to see how it all ties together, you can check out a closer look at Pattinson's new Batsuit. You can also read about how the sequel's fight scenes have been more challenging for the star, and why he says the movie will take things in "another totally different direction."

item.title: World of Warcraft: Forever looks like it could be a smash hit after the launch of the beta was overrun with eager fans, surprising even Blizzard itself.
item.description:
World of Warcraft: Forever looks like it could be a smash hit after the launch of the beta was overrun with eager fans, surprising even Blizzard itself.
Blizzard’s ended last weekend’s BlizzCon 2026 Opening Ceremony with the announcement of World of Warcraft: Forever, a “Classic Plus” MMO developed by the World of Warcraft Classic team, and set during the first year of World of Warcraft.
While Forever doesn’t launch until November 4, the beta was made available this week, and it was flooded by players. Those who did manage to get in faced disconnects. And then actually playing the game was tough due to extreme lag with looting and accepting quests. Hardly ideal.
World of Warcraft Classic developer Josh Greenfield took to X / Twitter to provide some insight into the popularity of the beta.
“Man, it was hard to sleep last night, I was so excited,” Greenfield said. “Beta has been... crazy. The craziest numbers I've seen in 17 years working at Blizzard and almost eight years on classic.
“We've got something really special here.”
That suggests significant interest in Forever, beyond even the launch of Classic itself. As a grizzled veteran of World of Warcraft’s early years, I remember well the brutal login queues most players would face when the groundbreaking MMO launched late 2004 and early 2005. Forever is rekindling those memories for me.
So, what’s going on with those queues? World of Warcraft senior game producer Tom Ellis took to X / Twitter to offer an explanation that acts as a fascinating insight into what goes on with the launch of an MMO. The upshot is this is a beta, and usually World of Warcraft betas don’t see this sort of interest.
“AHMAGERD, this game is 20 years old, how do you still suck at this!?! a. Heh, fair enough, short answer is, this is our BETA PTR environment stack, it's not a Production stack by a long, long, long, long, long, long shot. Betas for WoW aren't usually huge meter movers so this environment just isn't that powerful. This led to the first problem you saw today,” Ellis explained.
If you’ve got even a casual interest in online game infrastructure, Ellis’ post is worth a read. Ultimately, though, Blizzard sorted out the problems and the Forever beta is now running smoothly.
“Marked live once again and you all poured in without fuss,” he said. “Right now things are incredibly smooth for the first few hours of a public beta, Classic teams watching and fixing anything blocking that comes up but we're otherwise pretty much done for the night, enjoy!”
And that's what players are doing. I've seen multiple posts from fans praising the new visuals (in particular, the improved lighting), new sound effects (that rain!), and, from those who were there back in the day, the nostalgia-fueled trip down memory lane.
Wesley is Director, News at IGN. Find him on Twitter at @wyp100. You can reach Wesley at wesley_yinpoole@ign.com or confidentially at wyp100@proton.me.

item.title: Insomniac has released an update for Marvel’s Wolverine that nerfs the “fart gas” that had become such a talking point even before the game’s release.
item.description:
Insomniac has released an update for Marvel’s Wolverine that nerfs the “fart gas” that had become such a talking point even before the game’s release.
The debate around this was rekindled following the publication of Marvel’s Wolverine reviews earlier this month, with The Washington Post journalist Gene Park calling the scent trail “fart gas” because of the way it appears behind characters Logan follows.
Jean Grey’s fart gas trail is NOT part of the navigation assist option. i turned it on and there’s another green line that tells you where to go. mission waypoint (yellow marker) is on as well and THAT can be turned off.2nd pic i turn off the options and the gas stays. it seems… https://t.co/XSBsGa6Xj0 pic.twitter.com/cKs9uTPSG0
There was some confusion online about the ability to turn this feature off via accessibility options. Insomniac’s official list of accessibility options for Wolverine includes a “Chase Assist,” which lets you toggle reduced movement speed for targets during chase sequences, but it does not turn off the trail. Other navigation toggles do not turn off the scent trail either.
Ahead of Wolverine’s release, Insomniac’s director of community and marketing, James Stevenson, took to social media to explain that Logan's scent trail is baked into the way the mutant's powers work.
“The scent trail isn’t always on,” he clarified. “It represents Logan’s canon mutant super senses and elite tracking ability. It only is there when he’s tracking a specific scent / sound (a person, whisky, or another clue scent) - story/mission moments or when he catches whiff of a collectible.”
Referencing previous discourse about Final Fantasy’s yellow paint guides, some have said Logan's scent trails remove any potential skill required for chase sequences and any joy of discovery in exploration.
Then, earlier this week, Insomniac said it was planning to “further refine the player experience” based on feedback, while insisting it’s “incredibly proud” of the game. Most took that to mean it intended to tweak the “fart gas,” and so it has proved.
The patch notes, posted to Insomniac’s website, confirms the hotfix “adjusts the presentation of the Scent Trails and Audio Sense indicators, including reduced opacity to make these visuals less intense.”
So, the “fart gas” will feel less in your face from now on. But there’s more. Insomniac said it’s exploring adding toggleable options for a future update, which suggests players may eventually be able to turn off Scent Trails completely. Patch notes are below.
Sony has yet to announce an official sales figure for Marvel’s Wolverine, but early data suggests the PlayStation 5 exclusive sold 1.9 million copies in three days, generating around $130 million in revenue. We put that performance into context here.
Meanwhile, Marvel's Wolverine players are testing its motorcycle sequence to see if Logan can die if you don't touch the controller. Another player managed to take Logan out of bounds, revealing new areas of the game.
We’ve got 17 Essential Tips and Tricks to help you get started in Marvel’s Wolverine, plus our recommendations for the 10 Best Adaptations, and a guide on How to Farm XP Quickly. Check out our full Marvel’s Wolverine Walkthrough for a step-by-step guide to every mission, and make sure you don’t miss a thing with our Collectibles guides, All Wolverine Suits and Claws Guide, and our thorough list of all the Easter Eggs and References we've found.

item.title: A live-action Lollipop Chainsaw movie is officially in the works, developer Dragami Games has announced.
item.description:
A live-action Lollipop Chainsaw movie is officially in the works, developer Dragami Games has announced.
The studio behind the series revival announced plans to bring Juliet Starling to the big screen as part of Tokyo Game Show 2026, with full details shared by Deadline. It's yet another addition to the series as Dragami moves ahead with other previously announced installments, including an anime series and video game sequel.
The Lollipop Chainsaw movie will tell a prequel story set before the events of developer Grasshopper Manufacture's original bubblegum action game. It's also aimed to be an "R-rated action comedy" and will, once again, follow Juliet as the main character. Deadline also shared a brief story synopsis: "When a catastrophic zombie outbreak engulfs her school, Juliet must fight her way through the undead to save her friends, protect her family, and somehow keep her boyfriend Nick close – even if doing so ultimately requires some highly unconventional arrangements."
Dragami's film is said to be in development from an "international creative and production team" that includes Nada Holdings' Joe Teng, former ZDF Studios drama boss Robert Franke, Throne Inc MD Takafumi Yuki, Ambitious Entertainment's Kirk Shaw, and Non Stop TV's Patricio Rabuffetti. There is no word on whether original team members like Suda51 or now-DC Studios co-CEO James Gunn are involved, suggesting that, at least at this stage, they aren't attached in any capacity.
"We are truly excited to see our vision take another important step with the franchise’s first live-action feature film," Dragami president Shohei Sato said. "We are especially pleased to be working with such an experienced and passionate international team — one that understands what makes Lollipop Chainsaw special while embracing the opportunity to create something new."
Lollipop Chainsaw has been on a bit of a tear despite largely straying from the public eye for the last decade or so. Although it's firmly kept its place as a cult classic and fan-favorite Suda51 game, it wasn't until Dragami announced its RePop remaster in 2022 that Juliet started to turn heads once again. Whether an attempt to reanimate the franchise will succeed remains to be seen, though.
After RePop finally launched in 2024, Dragami announced plans to continue the series with new installments in the near future. The most recent peek at what exactly that entails actually arrived earlier this week with the reveal of Lollipop Chainsaw 2 Back2Back. First gameplay has revealed a project that looks both familiar and extremely different, leaving fans hesitant to see can stick the landing without Suda51 or Gunn's help.
The announcement that a Lollipop Chainsaw movie has encouraged similar responses from fans. For now, no information about the project's cast or release date has been revealed.
"We are making a film that feels unmistakably true to the spirit of Lollipop Chainsaw while standing completely on its own," Franke said. "Longtime fans will recognize the attitude, irreverence, and glorious excess they love, while newcomers can simply enjoy an unforgettable action-horror comedy. Our ambition is to create a film that entertains audiences everywhere, whether they’ve played the game or not."
It looks like we've got some waiting to do while Dragami revs up its Lollipop Chainsaw movie. Until then, you can read IGN's 5/10 review for the original game, where we said it "doesn’t even attempt to differentiate itself from the genre, and most of what it does try new in the realm of its characters and writing ultimately ends up taking away from an incredible-on-paper action game.
"The music and sidekick are really all you can rely on to stay great from start to finish. The rest of Lollipop Chainsaw is all over the place before it ultimately settles for mediocrity and disappointment."
Michael Cripe is a freelance writer with IGN. He's best known for his work at sites like The Pitch, The Escapist, and OnlySP. Be sure to give him a follow on Bluesky (@mikecripe.bsky.social) and Twitter (@MikeCripe).

item.title: Final Fantasy 7 Revelation will require around 200GB of storage when it launches next year, director Naoki Hamaguchi has warned.
item.description:
Final Fantasy 7 Revelation will require around 200GB of storage when it launches next year, director Naoki Hamaguchi has warned.
The Square Enix developer talked about the install requirements for the remake trilogy's long-awaited conclusion during an interview with VGC. When talking about how Final Fantasy 7 Revelation will compare to previous entries in the series, he confirmed that the final chapter of Cloud and Sephiroth's story will be especially demanding.
"Things are still getting worked out, but it’s probably going to be around 200GB of game," Hamaguchi said when asked about additional downloads for physical versions of Final Fantasy 7 Revelation. "I understand there are a lot of opinions about this topic, but at the end of the day, the fact is we need to overcome the hardware to a certain extent.
"One thing I want to say is, even though the game will not be on the full disc, in the position we’re in, because discs may be dying out, or maybe staying, with Final Fantasy 7 Revelation, we definitely wanted to deliver some kind of physical product. That was really important to us. Trust me!"
Managing installed games sometimes feels like packing a suitcase for a trip. Stuffing your chosen storage space with the essentials means having to choose what comes with you and what stays home, so when a big game comes along and asks to fill storage space with shiny new graphics and giant worlds to explore, hard decisions have to be made if you don't want to shell out the cash for more room. Individual install sizes often vary between platforms, but it's still something players have tried to learn to deal with as games grow increasingly complex.
It's a debacle Hamaguchi and the rest of the Square Enix team is surely aware of, but that doesn't mean anyone was willing to compromise the quality of Final Fantasy 7 Revelation. In a separate post on X/Twitter, Hamaguchi acknowledged that "a larger file size may not necessarily mean a better game," but there are other reasons to look forward to its 2027 release date.
"However, this title is the culmination of more than 10 years of work from our development team and serves as the conclusion to the FFVII Remake series," he said. "We are committed to delivering a game that not only meets the expectations of our fans, but is also a work that we, as creators, can be truly proud of."
Players will learn why Final Fantasy 7 Revelation takes up so much space when it launches for PC via the Epic Games Store and Steam, Nintendo Switch 2, PlayStation 5, and Xbox Series X/S come April 8, 2027. IGN already got a taste of what's to come and shared our findings in two recent previews.
For more, you can read our interview with Hamaguchi. You can also learn more about the game yourself by checking out what Square Enix had to show at gamescom 2026.
Michael Cripe is a freelance writer with IGN. He's best known for his work at sites like The Pitch, The Escapist, and OnlySP. Be sure to give him a follow on Bluesky (@mikecripe.bsky.social) and Twitter (@MikeCripe).

item.title: Developer Rebel Wolves' September success story, The Blood of Dawnwalker, reportedly cost just $40 million to make.
item.description:
Developer Rebel Wolves' September success story, The Blood of Dawnwalker, cost just $40 million to make.
Information related to the Warsaw, Poland-based studio's behind-the-scenes activities comes from a new Bloomberg report. It included the news that Rebel Wolves managed to bring The Blood of Dawnwalker to life and find a solid audience with little more than the $40 million budget supplied by NetEase Inc.
Game designer Konrad Tomaszkiewicz, who previously served as one of the leading developers behind games like The Witcher 3: Wild Hunt and Cyberpunk 2077, worked on early versions of Rebel Wolves' first game with a small team back in 2022. Tomaszkiewicz self-funded the project for that first year as the team hammered out its prototype in hopes of finding a partner, with NetEase later stepping in with the fund the game while acquiring 26% of the studio.
The $40 million figure comfortably lands The Blood of Dawnwalker in the AA space instead of the AAA realm where games often carry heftier price tags. For comparison, IO Interactive's 007 First Light reportedly carried a budget of more than $200 million. Sony's struggling Marathon game is said to have had a similar budget, with games like The Last of Us Part 2 and Horizon Forbidden West also reportedly in that range.
A relatively modest budget means the risk for Rebel Wolves, NetEase, and publisher Bandai Namco wasn't quite as great, but it doesn't seem to have had any impact on their game's achievements. Metacritic recorded that The Blood of Dawnwalker has received "Generally Favorable" reviews from both critics and users alike. IGN, for example, awarded it a 9/10, calling it "an impressive, bloody cocktail of interesting ideas and well-written characters, making it one of this year’s best open-world RPGs."
It's unclear just how successful The Blood of Dawnwalker has been since its launch for PC and consoles earlier this month, but a few clues have helped shed some light. Rebel Wolves told Bloomberg it is "extremely" happy with what it's seen so far, which includes reaching more than 1 million copies sold in just a few days. SteamDB has reported that player numbers for the single-player RPG are holding strong, too, with the game currently boasting a 24-hour peak of 24,495 concurrent users after hitting a peak of 78,188 shortly after launch.
Tomaszkiewicz told Bloomberg that his original goal was to keep Rebel Wolves from growing too much, but as ambitions grew, so did the team. The studio employed around 90 staff in 2024 but has since ballooned to encompass 160 members. Now, as they charge ahead on The Blood of Dawnwalker sequels and more, Tomaszkiewicz said they "don't want to overdo it."
"We decided that the size of the team we have right now is the most fitting for our needs," Tomaszkiewicz said. "It’s still letting me know everyone. I can speak with everyone every day. I still feel like a creator and not a manager, which is the place I want to be."
The Blood of Dawnwalker launched for PC, PlayStation 5, and Xbox Series X/S September 3, 2026. As work on more projects happens behind closed doors, more updates for Rebel Wolves' debut title are on the way, too. New Game Plus, for example, was recently confirmed to be in the works.
Michael Cripe is a freelance writer with IGN. He's best known for his work at sites like The Pitch, The Escapist, and OnlySP. Be sure to give him a follow on Bluesky (@mikecripe.bsky.social) and Twitter (@MikeCripe).

item.title: Remedy's games have always had Lynchian inspirations, including its new open-world action game Control Resonant.
item.description:
Remedy Entertainment's games have always been inspired by the late, great filmmaker David Lynch, who passed away in January 2025. Best known for the influential muder mystery series Twin Peaks and cult classic thriller Mulholland Drive, Lynch's penchant for merging surrealism with horror and absurism made him iconic as a director and screenwriter. Those inspirations are clearly seen in 2019's Control and especially in 2023's Alan Wake 2. Now, Remedy's latest game Control Resonant features an Easter egg that pays tribute to him with one of the most powerful quotes from Twin Peaks.
Throughout the open zones in Control Resonant, you'll find tons of details in the environment that build up its fictional version of New York City. One is a movie theater with a marquee outside that reads: "NOW PLAYING: FIX YOUR HEART OR DIE."
It's a reference to a line from 2017's Twin Peaks: The Return in which the character Gordon Cole (played by David Lynch himself) says the following to his transgender colleague Denise Bryson (played by David Duchovny):
"When I had you working undercover at the DEA, you were a confused and wild thing sometimes. I had enough dirt on you to fill the Grand Canyon. And I never used a spoonful because you were and are a great agent. And when you became Denise, I told all your colleagues, those clown comics, to fix their hearts or die."
Thus, the phrase "fix your heart or die" had become an iconic line not only in the Twin Peaks pantheon, highlighting the convictions of Lynch's character, but also a motto and rallying cry for transgender folks and in trans rights activism.
Bryson's depictation in the totality of Twin Peaks isn't without its problematic tropes, especially in the original 1990-1991 run, but Lynch's character (and Lynch himself) made it a point to make a statement against transphobia outright. And that resonated with many trans people.
It's really nice to see Remedy, through Control Resonant, pay homage to one of its biggest influences, but also make reference to a specific quote that now serves a specific purpose.
Be sure to check out my Control Resonant review, which I scored an 8, saying, "Even when combat's sharp edge eventually dulls, Control Resonant is a great addition to the Remedyverse. While its story follows a more standard framework, its gravitational pull is in the inventive world built around it and the humanization that grounds the paranatural intrigue." It published on September 18, 2026, and if you can believe it, that's a Friday once again.

item.title: Forget Batman and Superman. This massive Swamp Thing book might just be DC's most exciting upcoming release in 2027.
item.description:
DC Comics has released its full list of solicitations for December 2026. And while there's a lot to be excited for at the end of the year (including the impending finale of Tom King and Daniel Sampere's Wonder Woman run), the biggest news involves a new hardcover collection of Alan Moore's classic Saga of the Swamp Thing run.
The Swamp Thing by Alan Moore Omnibus promises to be the definitive collection of what most would regard as one of the finest comics ever published by DC. That's because this two-volume slipcase set will reprint the entirety of Moore's run with a restored and remastered version of the original coloring and period-appropriate paper stock.
For those not familiar, there are currently two ways of reading Moore's Swamp Thing in collected format, neither of which feature the original coloring from the single issues. The six trade paperbacks and two Absolute Edition hardcovers each have new, modernized coloring, and both versions have been heavily criticized by fans for altering the tone of the original comics.
You can check out this Reddit thread to see a side-by-side comparison of the originals, the trade paperbacks, and the Absolute Editions. The differences are pretty stark, to put it mildly. DC hasn't yet released any interior preview art of the Swamp Thing by Alan Moore Omnibus, but the expectation is that the books will be much more in line with how the series originally appeared in the '80s.
Here's DC's official summary of the Swamp Thing by Alan Moore Omnibus:

item.title: Games Workshop has released a new trailer for Astartes II, the most anticipated Warhammer 40,000 animation ever.
item.description:
Games Workshop has released a new trailer for Astartes II, the most anticipated Warhammer 40,000 animation ever.
For the uninitiated, the original Astartes was created by superfan Syama Pedersen, who was subsequently brought into the fold to make the official sequel. Astartes is widely accepted as the greatest Warhammer 40,000 animation ever made, official or unofficial, with only Amazon’s excellent Space Marine 2 animation for the Secret Level anthology series competing with it in quality terms. Indeed, Astartes was so good that it inspired Saber Interactive’s hugely successful Space Marine 2 in terms of the look and feel of the Space Marines themselves.
During Games Workshop’s ‘Big Autumn Preview’ event, fans were treated to a new look at Astartes II, which confirms the appearance of Deathwatch and Terminators. As the company notes in a post on Warhammer Community, fans of Space Hulk will no doubt find a lot familiar here.
ASTARTES 2 teaserComing DecemberWe get to follow a Deathwatch unit investigating a Space Hulk! pic.twitter.com/DgveN5yz6K
Indeed, the Space Hulk vibes come through loud and clear. We see Space Marines stomp about a dark, shadowy interior which you just know will house horrible, nightmarish things in the shadows. But the first-person shot of a corridor lit only by spotlights is the clearest sign that the much-loved tabletop game, Space Hulk, was an influence.
Also in the post, Games Workshop confirmed that Astartes II will be “significantly longer” than its predecessor, which is music to fan ears. Understandably as a single-person fan project, Astartes is on the short side.
“We knew already that this was likely to feature Deathwatch and Terminators, from the unsubtle hints dropped at the end of the LAST trailer, and now we see them, they look like they mean business,” Games Workshop said. “The imposing line of storm bolter barrels and the crackle of a power fist, combined with the ominous surroundings, are certainly giving off some strong Space Hulk vibes.
“Somehow even more intimidating than the blank visage of the Terminator helms is that unhelmeted Space Marine veteran, who could certainly be described as ‘grizzled.’ And we think we clocked at least three different characters and Chapters of Space Marines in that trailer.”
In November last year, Games Workshop revealed animation work on a monitor screen via the promo video, below, that showed a squad of Terminators appearing to protect an unnamed human soldier. This was the Inquisition-led Deathwatch Terminator squad from the debut Astartes 2 teaser in incomplete form, but we know from their pauldron chapter symbols that they’re the same as before (Retributors, Mortifactors, Scythes of The Emperor, Sons of Medusa, and Angels Vermilion).
Last year’s teaser suggested an animation on a scale and quality never-before-seen from Warhammer 40,000, with melee combat, shooting, vehicle combat, and even spaceship battles all showcased. It showed a number of Space Marine chapters in battle across varied environments, and multiple enemy races, including Tyranids, Orks, and Tau.
But it turned out that nothing in the teaser is actually in the Astartes 2 animation itself. According to a post on the Warhammer Community website: “This teaser trailer is not actually clips from the new animation, instead showing a compilation of shots that represent the former lives of the characters that will appear in the show. There’s a pretty unsubtle hint at the end as to the nature of the final story... We’ll leave you to speculate and start putting the pieces together yourselves.”
Astartes II is due out this December on Warhammer+, Games Workshop’s streaming service.
Wesley is Director, News at IGN. Find him on Twitter at @wyp100. You can reach Wesley at wesley_yinpoole@ign.com or confidentially at wyp100@proton.me.

item.title: Paramount's World War Z sequel is moving forward, with Brad Pitt confirmed to return and Conclave's Edward Berger attached to direct.
item.description:
Paramount's World War Z sequel is moving forward, with Brad Pitt confirmed to return and Conclave's Edward Berger attached to direct.
It's two major updates for the post-apocalyptic zombie follow-up that arrived via Deadline. The site said that deals are closed, confirming that World War Z 2 – or whatever it ends up being called – has already nailed down two of the biggest question marks following its announcement in April of this year.
Deadline also reported that Plan B Entertainment's Pitt, Dede Gardner, and Jeremy Kleiner will produce, with Berger also in the mix as an executive producer. Another update is that Dennis Kelly, the creator of TV series Utopia and writer behind 2021's Together, will pen the World War Z sequel's script. It otherwise still seems to be in the early days for the project, as no additional details regarding its plot, release date, or casting have been revealed.
The World War Z IP is being reheated 13 years after the original film successfully introduced audiences to a live-action adaptation of Max Brooks' 2000s novel. Pitt starred in the first film and has expressed interest in returning to the franchise for some time, but getting it off the ground and back into the zombie horde has proven to be quite the challenge for the last decade. As his roles in movies like Once Upon a Time in... Hollywood and F1 have come and gone, so too have hopes for the sequel.
Issues with confirming a director aside, fans started to expect that a follow-up would never come to be when Paramount put it on the back burner in 2019. The Social Network and Zodiac director David Fincher was even said to be involved at one point, but despite him comparing his ideas for a take to The Last of Us, that version of World War Z never materialized. Berger has now taken the reins.
Berger turned heads when Conclave premiered in 2024, but he's got more than just the Ralph Fiennes movie under his belt. He also directed 2022's critically acclaimed war film All Quiet on the Western Front, as well as 2014's Jack. He's also said to be involved with Matt Damon's new Jason Bourne movie, though that particular project's status is somewhat of a mystery.
The specifics surrounding Pitt's return to World War Z are unclear. Although the events of the first film could put his character, Gerry Lane, front and center once again, story information has not been revealed. When World War Z 2 does come out, it will mark a reunion for Pitt and Berger, who recently worked together on The Riders. Deadline reported that the former pitched the idea of more World War Z to the latter while working on the project, with the pair ready to get to get back to work by the time production came to an end.
The World War Z sequel has no release date, but at the speed things are moving at now, it may not be too long before we hear more. While we wait, you can read IGN's 7.6/10 review for the original movie, which earned $540 million at the box office (via Box Office Mojo). You can also see why the developers behind the World War Z video game might feel at least partially responsible for the existence of a sequel.
Photo by Jason Kempin/Getty Images.

item.title: A new species of small, spotted wild cat -- leopardus tilcayo or the tilcayo tiger cat -- was discovered in Bolivia where it been mistaken by the man who took it in as a kitten.
item.description:
A new breed of cat has been discovered for the first time in 100 years.
Citing the journal Current Biology, NBC News reports that a new wild cat species dubbed leopardus tilcayo (or the tilcayo tiger cat) was discovered in the Bolivian Yungas. The exact size of this particular cat population in the wild remains unclear.
The tilcayo tiger cat is smaller than the average house cat, has rounded ears, a slender build, and is spotted.
A new species of cat has been identified for the first time in a century—and experts think that there may be even more to discover around the world: https://t.co/woOXXxJOXB pic.twitter.com/OX12m8wV3V
Paola Nogales-Ascarrunz, the co-author of Current Biology’s study, came upon the cat while volunteering for a wildlife rehabilitation center in Bolivia and thought it looked just different enough to warrant further investigation.
“The cat had been brought in by a man living in a community in the forest near La Paz who had mistaken the cat for a domestic kitten, according to details recorded by the sanctuary,” NBC reports. “He had fed the animal noodles, rice and eggs, only to realize it was wild and that he could not take care of it. So he brought it to the sanctuary.”
It was originally believed to have been a known species of wild cat, but Nogales-Ascarrunz conducted genetic testing that ultimately determined this was its own distinct cat species.
While leopardus tilcayo may be a new discovery for researchers, its existence is old news to local peoples in Bolivia who have been aware of its existence for years.
Scientists have discovered a new species of cat for the first time in over a century.Smaller than an average housecat and covered in leopard-like spots, the cat species — proposed name Leopardus tilcayo — lives in Bolivia’s Yungas forest ecoregion. Very little is known about… pic.twitter.com/2dFDkgDzKi
“This cat, they call it tilcayo. And when you ask, ‘Does it have some meaning in Quechua or Almyra and other Indigenous languages?’ they say, ‘No, my grandpa told me that’s the tilcayo,’” Nogales-Ascarrunz said. “This is a traditional knowledge that they have in the community. We want to preserve that knowledge and we didn’t want to give it another name.”
Nogales-Ascarrunz’s biggest concern about the little cat is preserving the species’ existence. The five tiger cat species native to Central and South America exist in habitats where conservation is already imperiled by development and the expansion of agriculture.

item.title: Reacher star Alan Ritchson is reportedly in talks to star in PlayStation's upcoming Helldivers movie.
item.description:
Reacher star Alan Ritchson is reportedly in talks to star in PlayStation's upcoming Helldivers movie.
As reported by Deadline, the feature film adaptation of Arrowhead Game Studios' brutal multiplayer hit is zeroing in on a new lead after Aquaman actor Jason Momoa exited the project earlier this year. Ritchson is only said to be in talks for the unnamed Helldivers role so far, but Sony and director Justin Lin will want to move fast if they still want to hit their video game-to-movie adaptation's November 2027 drop date.
Ritchson has emerged as one of the more memorable action faces in the last decade. Although he's best known as the face of Prime Video's Reacher series, he's also shown up in Supergirl, Titans, and Fast X. Most recently, viewers may recognize him from his work in Netflix's War Machine or in this month's Owen Wilson movie, Runner.
Plot details for the Helldivers movie remain tightly under wraps as the crew tries to pin Ritchson behind the scenes. Sony announced plans to bring the battle for Super Earth to the big screen back in January 2025, and although things seemed to be progressing smoothly enough since, a few snags have kept it from landing.
For example, Lin, the director behind some The Fast and the Furious movies, boarded Helldivers in December of last year. Momoa then followed as Sony nailed down a release date in February of this year.
As much sense as it would make to see Momoa buzzing through Terminids and Automatons in the name of liberty, the DC and Game of Thrones star was said to have bailed on Helldivers in June. Why he departed the movie still remains unclear, though fans probably aren't too beaten up over the idea now that Ritchson could be the one to suit up.
Helldivers is still careening toward its November 10, 2027, theatrical release date. While Sony and Ritchson hammer out the details, you can read about how Arrowhead is involved in the production and what its CEO had to say to the director.

item.title: IGN can exclusively reveal that the first-ever public screening of Hirayasumi Anime will take place during a one-night event on October 7 at New York City's Japan Society, giving fans an early look at Episode 1 before the series officially debuts in 2027.
item.description:
IGN can exclusively reveal that the first-ever public screening of Hirayasumi Anime will take place during a one-night event on October 7 at New York City's Japan Society, giving fans an early look at Episode 1 before the series officially debuts in 2027.
The event will kick off at 7pm ET, and the night will also feature a panel where composer Kaori Sawada, producer Junichi Katsutani, and VIZ Media's Godswill Ugwa will discuss what it was like bringing the acclaimed manga to the screen.
If you'd like to attend, you can grab tickets right here!
For those unfamiliar, Hirayasumi has been a huge global success and has been serialized in Weekly Big Comic Spirits since 2021. The manga has more than 1.7 million copies in circulation worldwide across ten volumes, and it was the recipient of the 71st Shogakukan Manga Award alongside being named Best Serial Comic at Lucca Comics & Games 2024.
"At 29 years old, carefree Hiroto Ikuta doesn’t have a girlfriend, a full-time job, or a plan for the future—and he couldn’t be happier," Hirayasumi's official description reads. "Hiroto’s breezy attitude isn’t easy for everyone to understand, though. In a world filled with anxiety, confusion, and grief, Hiroto and the people around him are all just doing their best to figure out this thing called life."
Once again, fans interested in attending the event can grab their tickets right here, and you can also watch the anime's official teaser trailer below.

item.title: Zach Cregger's Resident Evil is out today, and it's already the highest-rated video game movie of all time on Rotten Tomatoes.
item.description:
Zach Cregger's Resident Evil is out today, and it's already the highest-rated video game movie of all time on Rotten Tomatoes.
The scores are in, and at least as far as the review-aggregating website is concerned, the latest shot at a live-action adaptation of Capcom's beloved survival horror series has received the best reaction of any game movie to date. Resident Evil, which was directed by Weapons' Cregger and stars Austin Abrams, boasts a 96% critics' rating at the time of this story's publication, placing it multiple percentage points above a shortlist of other well-received adaptations, including Sonic the Hedgehog 3 (86%), Werewolves Within (86%), and The Angry Birds Movie 2 (72%).
Video games have a long history of what has been deemed by many to be mediocre releases. Although many of those — including 2001's Tomb Raider and 1993's Super Mario Bros. — arrived early in the industry's life, recent years have had their fill of poorly received projects, too. Both Five Nights at Freddy's movies, despite pulling in plenty of love from audiences, failed to impress critics, and 2024's Borderlands fell just 11 places short of being the worst-rated video game movie of all time. What we're saying is that it's not exactly been stiff competition for Resident Evil, but don't let that dampen its impact.
Despite Cregger making a splash with his last two horror movies, the director has faced an uphill battle with his latest flick. Fans expecting the movie to stick closer to the lore were let down to see Abrams playing an original character in a live-action Raccoon City that looked a bit different than they may have been hoping for. Instead of Leon S. Kennedy, Nemesis, or any other familiar elements, the live-action Resident Evil instead opted to focus on new character Bryan in a story inspired by the feeling of playing the games rather than their stories.
"I did not really appreciate the sentiment that, ‘We’ve been waiting forever for Leon’s story.’ And I appreciate that, and I’m sorry that’s not the story I’m bringing," Cregger said during a recent conversation with IGN. "I get it, I understand the frustration. I understand it so well because I haven’t seen the earlier [Resident Evil] movies, because they don't look like the Resident Evil that I love, so how could I be frustrated with fans who have that same attitude?"
It's been controversial, to say the least, but despite the online backlash that's seeped into Cregger's world, the critics aren't the only ones finding something to love about Resident Evil. After more than 500 verified ratings, Rotten Tomatoes has recorded a staggering 91% score from audiences. Whatever hangups you may have thought audiences would have going in, it seems the film has proven too good for most to deny.
"My only hope is that they’ll see the movie regardless of their skepticism or their disappointment that I’m not telling some of the stories that the games tell so well, and they will feel seen when they do watch the movie, and they will recognize all of the love for the games that are in this movie, because it is there," Cregger added during his talk with IGN. "This is not me just telling a story and slapping Resident Evil on it so I can get a budget. This is me telling a Resident Evil story."
Resident Evil is still just getting its feet wet when it comes to its reception, so only time will tell if it will continue to be seen in a positive light in the weeks, months, and years ahead. It's undeniably a strong start, though, with the project also expected to clear the franchise's box office record.
IGN gave it a solid rating, too, awarding it an 8/10 review. We said, "With a laser focus on putting its hero through the worst night of his life, Resident Evil is a simple and exciting survival horror story that benefits greatly from director Zach Cregger’s sensibilities."
Michael Cripe is a freelance writer with IGN. He's best known for his work at sites like The Pitch, The Escapist, and OnlySP. Be sure to give him a follow on Bluesky (@mikecripe.bsky.social) and Twitter (@MikeCripe).

item.description:
Toys 'R' Us, the once-ubiquitous toy store/mecca for 1980s kids, is set to open 120 new standalone stores this holiday season, the company announced. The expansion is in partnership with the Go! Retail Group, who first partnered with Toys 'R' Us owner WHP Global three years ago to begin the toy store back from the dead and back into retail life. There are currently 40 standalone stores nationwide as well as other locations inside select Macy's locations nationwide.
"This is a major moment for Toys 'R' Us as we significantly expand our presence across the United States," said WHP Global Executive Vice President Jamie Uitdenhowen. "Together with our incredible partners, we are growing Toys' R' Us in unique ways to meet customers wherever they are, whether that's at a standalone store in their hometown, inside Macy's, at the airport or at a Navy Exchange."
"This holiday season represents an extraordinary expansion for Toys 'R' Us in the US, and we couldn't be more excited to bring the magic of Toys'R'Us to so many communities across the country," said Gideon Schlessinger, CEO of Go! Retail Group. "There's something special about walking into a Toys'R'Us store, especially during the holidays — the excitement of discovering the hottest toys, seeing favorite brands and characters come to life, and finding that perfect gift."
This 40-something writer has fond memories wandering the seemingly endless aisles of toys in the store as a kid – in particularly the video game aisle, which had the game box art on the walls and tickets below each one, which you'd take to a special counter if you wanted to buy the game and they'd get the real thing from a lockup area in the back for you. But the Toys 'R' Us revival will attempt to modernize the chain as well.
"Select locations will introduce new experiences at the intersection of play, entertainment and content creation, including Creator Studios, dedicated spaces where influencers, creators and toy brands can create content, unveil new products and host toy reveals, launches and special events," the company said. "Select stores will also feature candy shops and cafés, giving customers even more reasons to explore, discover and spend time at Toys 'R' Us."

item.title: After putting up the Steam Frame for reservation on Monday, Valve has finally sent out its emails letting people know if they're on the reservation list or on the waitlist for the new VR headset. And, predictably, scalpers are already listing Steam Frame reservations on eBay.
item.description:
After putting up the Steam Frame for reservation on Monday, Valve has finally sent out its emails letting people know if they're on the reservation list or on the waitlist for the new VR headset. And, predictably, scalpers are already listing Steam Frame reservations on eBay.
While Valve lists the 256GB Steam Frame kit for $1,059, the eBay listings start at $1,700 for the lower storage tier. If you want to get the 1TB model, that's being listed at around $2,000 by scalpers, despite Valve's $1,299 asking price.
What's especially egregious about these listings is that the Steam Frame is already expensive for what it is, due to the ongoing RAM crisis. While I'd have some wiggle room for a VR headset with Valve's open platform and incredible wireless PCVR, I'm not sure I'd spend that much money on something without OLED optics.
Unfortunately, it looks like at least some of these listings have already sold.
Luckily, the community is fighting back. Folks on the /r/steam subreddit are mobilizing to report these listings, and it seems like eBay is taking action. After sharing instructions on how to report these listings, user /u/obscenemexican added: "Update: I'm now getting flooded with emails from eBay that the reported content has been removed, huzzah! Many down, many more to go, keep it up guys!"
Meanwhile, other users in the thread have found some of the scalpers' Steam usernames in the eBay listings and have reported them to Valve. User /u/noonyIRL said: "If you want to hurt these scum more, contact them and ask for the Steam ID tied to the reservation to check their VAC/Ban status to ensure its legitimate. If they provide it, report them to Valve, if they refuse, report to eBay for failing to provide suitable evidence. Either way, this hits their account, not just their listing."
Valve did try to mitigate the risks of scalpers when it released both the Steam Machine and the Steam Frame, implementing a random lottery system tied to its preorders. When the Frame was announced on Monday, Valve opened up a sign-up system, where anyone with a Steam Account could select which version of the headset they were interested in. Then, Valve randomized the entries and split them into a bucket of reservations and a waitlist.
I'm sure that did mitigate how many scalpers would otherwise be able to get the system if it was available on a first-come, first-serve basis, but it clearly did not stop scalpers from trying to profit off of the system's scarcity. Hopefully, either eBay, Valve or both get this situation under control, so that more people are able to get the Frame at a somewhat reasonable cost.
Jackie Thomas is the Senior Tech Editor at IGN and the PC components queen. She's been covering gaming hardware for more than a decade for IGN, TechRadar, Gizmodo, PC Gamer and more. You can follow her @Jackiecobra

item.title: Former PlayStation executives Shuhei Yoshida and Adam Boyes have recreated their iconic game-sharing instructional video as Sony helps the industry barrel toward a discless future.
item.description:
Former PlayStation executives Shuhei Yoshida and Adam Boyes have recreated their iconic game-sharing instructional video as Sony helps the industry barrel toward a discless future.
Even if you weren't playing too many games in 2013, there's a good chance you remember the "Official PlayStation Used Game Instructional Video." It was a viral 20-second how-to that saw then-Sony figureheads Boyes and Yoshida deliver a tongue-in-cheek guide for sharing physical games on PS4, racking up 21.3 million YouTube views in the 13 years since its premiere.
At the time, Sony took a clear and successful jab at Microsoft and its rocky Xbox One launch plans. Fast forward 13 years, and Sony's plan to kill physical discs will have game sharing on PlayStation looking quite different from 2028. With the end of physical discs looming, Boyes and Yoshida reunited to recreate the legendary moment at Tokyo Game Show, and unfortunately, there were no physical games to be found.
Met with a best friend :D @amboyes @PlayStation_jp #TGS2026 pic.twitter.com/2ZjsrLMNaP
"Met with a best friend," Yoshida said with an open-smile emoticon.
The two snapped a few photos together as part of Tokyo Game Show, calling back to the moment that has lived rent-free in gamers' heads for years. It was clearly a fun nod to PlayStation's past, but the future is looking grim, and fans have mixed feelings.
"This picture of Shuhei Yoshida and Adam Boyes from Tokyo Game Show is making the rounds," physical game X/Twitter account @DoesItPlay1 said. "Seemingly mocking current anti-consumer PlayStation for killing the philosophy behind their once famous pro-consumer mockery of Xbox regarding physical game sharing."
"This is how you share games with your friends in 2028," another fan added, referencing the lack of games in their hands.
How it started / How it ended pic.twitter.com/pXBz5lUbQQ
I know what you did there. pic.twitter.com/d6AztR0uIC
2013 vs 2026 🥲13 ans plus tard, Shuhei Yoshida recrée sur son compte Twitter sa photo iconique de l’E3 2013… sauf que cette fois, lui et son collègue ne s’échangent que du vent !#TokyoGameShow #PlayStation pic.twitter.com/fkJEq5yu2L
Sony announced in July of this year that it would cease physical disc production for new video games starting in January 2028. It's a move that has landed the PlayStation company in hot water for months, and despite recently soft sales for game discs, the topic isn't something fans plan to let go anytime soon.
But in July, Sony insisted its decision wasn't having any impact on its business, and it didn't predict any negative impact in the future, either. When Sony announced the news it said it was simply following consumer trends. “In response to shifting trends in consumer preference, new games will be released on PlayStation Store and at retailers in digital formats only,” Sid Shuman, Senior Director, Sony Interactive Entertainment Content Communications, said in a post on PlayStation Blog.
There are of course instances of companies reversing controversial decisions amid a backlash, but, as analysts have told IGN, it remains unlikely that Sony will U-turn on this. For Sony, going all-digital for new game releases will earn it more money from every sale at a time when console sales are expected to plummet due to their rising cost.
For a first-party PlayStation game such as Marvel's wolverine, Sony will only keep around 65% of the money from a physical copy, with around 30% going to the retailer and roughly another 5% on manufacturing costs. Meanwhile, for a physical copy of a third-party game such as the Activision-published Call of Duty, Sony will get a licensing fee, likely around 15%.
As Microsoft introduces a new feature that will allow Xbox players to digitize their physical games, it's hard not to look at the irony of where game sharing is at in 2026. While we wait to see how it all shakes out, you can read why one IGN writer called Sony's decision both concerning and offensive.
Michael Cripe is a freelance writer with IGN. He's best known for his work at sites like The Pitch, The Escapist, and OnlySP. Be sure to give him a follow on Bluesky (@mikecripe.bsky.social) and Twitter (@MikeCripe).

item.title: Sony has yet to announce an official sales figure for Marvel’s Wolverine, but one analyst has said early data suggests it's sold 1.9 million copies since going on sale on September 15, generating around $130 million in revenue.
item.description:
Sony has yet to announce an official sales figure for Marvel’s Wolverine, but one analyst has said early data suggests it's sold 1.9 million copies since going on sale on September 15, generating around $130 million in revenue.
Rhys Elliott, head of market analysis at Alinea Analytics, took to social media to say an estimated 22.9% of that revenue came from the sale of physical copies of the game — remember, Sony plans to cease production of PlayStation discs from 2028.
Through all this, it’s important to note that Sony has yet to make any official sales announcement for Marvel’s Wolverine. It has made sales announcements for PlayStation Studios games in the past. For example, Sucker Punch’s Ghost of Yotei went on sale on October 2, 2025 and sold 3.3 million units as of November 2 (at the 32 day mark), according to Sony’s official figures.
Back in October 2023, Sony announced that Insomniac's PlayStation 5 exclusive Spider-Man 2 sold more than 2.5 million copies in 24 hours, which meant the open-world superhero game overtook Santa Monica Studio’s God of War Ragnarok at the top of the PlayStation day-one launch sales chart. At the time, it was the fastest-selling PlayStation Studios game in history (Helldivers 2 now holds top spot).
Assuming Alinea Analytics is in the right ballpark, Marvel’s Wolverine is tracking behind Spider-Man 2. But it has already passed the lifetime PS5 copies sold and revenues of Hideo Kojima’s Death Stranding 2, which hit the headlines when Sony ditched Kojima’s Physint. Indeed, according to Elliot, Marvel’s Wolverine is after just a few days on sale the top-performing new PlayStation Studios game released on PS5 so far this year, ahead of MLB The Show, Bungie’s Marathon, Housemarque’s Saros, and fighting game Marvel Tōkon.
The big question is how well Wolverine continues to sell. Wolverine is currently sitting on a 77 Metascore, with IGN’s Marvel’s Wolverine review returning a 6/10. We said: “Marvel's Wolverine's slick and satisfying combat wears thin well before its conclusion, so much so that even its strong character work can't quite save it from being anything more than okay.”
“So yes, Wolverine has sold well, but its commercial long tail is limited by its mixed media and streamer reception,” Elliott said. “Unlike Spider-Man, which reviewed insanely well and has stayed evergreen for years, this one’s tail will be shorter and lumpier, but still there.”
Expect a bump when the MCU kicks into gear this December with the release of Avengers: Doomsday, which features the X-Men (but does it feature Hugh Jackman’s Wolverine?). Wolverine might also benefit from the expanded PS5 install base that will inevitably kick in with the release of GTA 6 in November. And Wolverine is sure to prove a popular choice under the Christmas tree.
“Wolverine will keep selling, just not at Spider-Man heights,” Elliott added. “Spidey’s been evergreen. Wolverine will be more ever-yellow.”
Earlier this week, Insomniac said it was planning to “further refine the player experience” based on feedback. One aspect Insomniac may be looking at is Wolverine’s infamous “fart gas,” which has become the butt of online jokes in recent weeks. Some have called for Insomniac to add the ability to disable Logan’s scent trail entirely from the game amid complaints about handholding.
Meanwhile, Marvel's Wolverine players are testing its motorcycle sequence to see if Logan can die if you don't touch the controller. Another player managed to take Logan out of bounds, revealing new areas of the game.
